cells.question: Q01

passages.locator: Article 53(1), chapeau (same words as in Article 101(1), dataset quote aia-art101-gpai-fines)
passages.quote: providers of general-purpose AI models
shall be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk if it meets any of the following conditions

cells.note: The duties in Article 53 fall on providers of general-purpose AI models; Article 55(1) adds duties for providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, the category defined in Article 51 (high-impact capabilities, presumed above a training-compute threshold, or a Commission decision). Article 54 adds an authorised-representative duty for providers established in third countries; Article 53(2) exempts certain open-source models from points (a) and (b), but not models with systemic risk. 'Provider' is defined in Article 3(3) (not quoted).

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: presumed to have high impact capabilities pursuant to paragraph 1, point (a), when the cumulative amount of computation used for its training measured in floating point operations is greater than
greater than 1025
based on a decision of the Commission, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel

cells.note: The figure is 10 to the power 25 floating point operations; the cached text renders the superscript as '1025'. The compute figure is a presumption of high-impact capabilities under Article 51(1)(a); a model can also be classified by Commission decision having regard to the Annex XIII criteria. Article 51(3) empowers the Commission to amend the thresholds by delegated act; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1, point (37), restates that delegation in Article 97 without changing Article 51. Articles 52(2) to 52(5) provide for rebuttal and reassessment.

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level

cells.note: Providers of models with systemic risk must assess and mitigate systemic risks; Articles 53 and 55 do not require a written risk framework, policy or protocol. The only written policy required (Article 53(1)(c)) concerns copyright.

search.read: Chapter V (Articles 51 to 56), Article 3 points (63) to (65), Annexes XI to XIII; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Article 1 (all points) for amendments to these provisions

setAside.reason: A policy on copyright and related rights, a single other subject.
Risk management system for high-risk AI systems, not general-purpose AI models.
Technical documentation content (description of evaluation strategies), not a risk framework.

cells.question: Q04
cells.note: Not applicable: Q03 finds a risk-management duty but no written framework document, and the Q04 criterion is not applicable where Q03 finds no such document. Technical documentation, which includes evaluation strategies for models with systemic risk, is kept for supply to the AI Office on request (Article 53(1)(a), Annex XI); it is recorded under Q08.

setAside.locator: Article 53(1), point (a), and Annex XI, Section 2
setAside.reason: Technical documentation on the model, supplied to the AI Office on request; not a risk framework (see Q08).
Commission power to request the documentation drawn up under Articles 53 and 55; not a duty to publish or submit a framework.
Commission publishes a list of models with systemic risk, not providers' documents.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing

cells.note: Applies to providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk. The provision does not tie the evaluation to a point before or after the model is placed on the market.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned
through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code

cells.note: A power, not a requirement: the AI Office may evaluate a model to assess compliance where information under Article 91 is insufficient, or to investigate systemic risks; under Article 92(2) the Commission may appoint independent experts to carry out evaluations. Article 55(1)(a) requires adversarial testing but does not require that it be done by an external party.

search.read: Articles 55, 56, 88 to 94; Annex XI; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Article 1, point (21)

setAside.reason: Asks for a description of internal and/or external adversarial testing 'where applicable'; does not require external testing.

setAside.locator: Article 56(6) as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1, point (21)
setAside.reason: Commission assessment of the adequacy of codes of practice, not of a model or a provider's practices.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: report, without undue delay, to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents

cells.note: Applies to providers of models with systemic risk. The timing is 'without undue delay'; no number of days is set in the Regulation. 'Serious incident' is defined in Article 3(49) by reference to an AI system (not quoted).

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model
to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems
a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model, according to a template provided by the AI Office

cells.note: The technical documentation (Annex XI, with added items for models with systemic risk) is kept for supply to the AI Office and national competent authorities on request; information for downstream providers (Annex XII) is made available to them; the training-content summary is made publicly available. Points (a) and (b) do not apply to qualifying open-source models without systemic risk (Article 53(2)). Article 52(1) separately requires notification to the Commission within two weeks once the Article 51(1)(a) condition is met. No labelling duty for model outputs is among the provisions compared (Article 50 concerns AI systems).

cells.question: Q09

cells.note: Article 87 applies Directive (EU) 2019/1937 to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of reporting persons; the protections are set by that Directive, which is not read here. Article 89(2) gives downstream providers a right to lodge a complaint, a complaint mechanism that does not meet the criterion. Partly because the protection is applied by reference to another law, not stated in this Regulation.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101
It shall apply from 2 August 2026.
shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with the obligations laid down in this Regulation by 2 August 2027

cells.note: Chapter V duties apply from 2 August 2025. Article 101 (fines) is excepted from that date; read with the general date in the second paragraph, it applies from 2 August 2026. The text states no separate date for Article 101; this is a reading of the two quoted provisions. Under Article 111(3), providers of models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1, point (40), amends Article 113 points (a) and (c) and adds point (d), but leaves point (b) unchanged.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher

cells.note: The maximum is the higher of 3 % of annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, where the Commission finds that the provider intentionally or negligently infringed the relevant provisions or failed to comply with requests, measures or access for evaluation (Article 101(1)(a) to (d)). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 does not amend Article 101; its new SMC paragraph 6a applies to Article 99.

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines
The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned
The Commission has exclusive competence as regards general-purpose AI models under Article 88 of that Regulation.

cells.note: Under Article 88(1) the Commission has exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V and entrusts these tasks to the AI Office; Articles 89 to 93 give the AI Office and Commission monitoring, information, evaluation and measure powers. The new Article 75(1) inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 concerns AI systems, not models, and is not used here.

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance
shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission

passages.locator: Article 1, point (21), replacing Article 56(6) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
passages.quote: The Commission, taking utmost account of the opinion of the Board, shall assess whether the codes of practice cover the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55

cells.note: 'May rely on' codes of practice, until a harmonised standard is published (Articles 53(4) and 55(2)); compliance with European harmonised standards grants a presumption of conformity to the extent they cover the obligations. findings.statement: Within the searches stated below, no UK law or other binding instrument placing duties on developers of frontier or general-purpose AI models was located; this is not a finding that no such instrument exists. The 2024 King's Speech said the government would seek such legislation; the 2026 briefing notes contain none of the searched terms; the memoranda with developers state that they are not legally binding; and title searches of legislation.gov.uk for 2023–2026 found one instrument with "artificial intelligence" in its title, which places a duty on the Information Commissioner, not on developers.
